summary: A tab list and its panels, built on react-aria's tab collection. Children are TabItem.
useWhen: one region of the page shows one of several peer views, and only one at a time
the views are peers — no ordering, no progression between them

useInstead.when: the steps must be completed in order
useInstead.why: tabs imply peers you may visit in any order; a wizard is a sequence

useInstead.when: the sections should all be readable at once, or printable
useInstead.why: tabs hide everything but the active panel, including from Ctrl-F

useInstead.when: it is navigation between pages rather than panels within one

composition.note: TabItem comes from react-stately's collection Item — it takes no props of its own beyond `title` (the tab label) and `key`; its children are the panel.

pill.use: the default — a filled track, for switching views inside a panel or card

underline.use: a rule under the active tab, for page-level sections

vertical.use: a stacked track with up/down arrow keys
vertical.caveat: keyboard and ARIA are complete, but the decoration is not — the underline rule and the pill track's padding are still written for the horizontal axis. Figma has not specified the vertical drawing

guarantees: roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation and the aria-controls/aria-labelledby pairing between each tab and its panel come from react-aria
the focus ring shows for keyboard focus only, and hover does not latch on touch
requires: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on Tabs — the tab list is a named region

antiPatterns.dont: tabs whose panels the user must read in order
antiPatterns.why: the role announces peers, and nothing stops a user landing on the last one first

antiPatterns.dont: hiding required form fields behind a tab
antiPatterns.why: a validation error in an inactive panel is invisible; the user is told the form is invalid with nothing on screen to fix
a tablist with a single tab is chrome with no choice in it
